html:
The retornados were the Portuguese settlers who came back from the African colonies, above all Angola and Mozambique, when those became independent after the Carnation Revolution.

In 1975, as civil war broke out in Angola, an airlift brought tens of thousands to Lisbon, and ships brought their goods. In all perhaps half a million people arrived within a short time, in a country of under ten million. Many had never lived in Portugal and arrived with nothing.

The state housed them in hotels and helped with loans. Most found work and settled, and many started businesses. The retornados changed Portuguese society and brought African influences with them, as did later migrants from Cape Verde and Angola. It ended five centuries of empire that began at Ceuta.
sum: The retornados were the Portuguese settlers who came back from the African colonies, above all Angola and Mozambique, when those became independent after the Carnation Revolution.
